🎯 Why I Built Google Antigravity Science Plugin Cookbook & 3D Biomolecular Studio (Engineering Purpose & Real-World Value) ### 1. 🧬 Bridging Agentic Coding with Computational Biology I created this cookbook to show how autonomous AI agents can orchestrate real scientific workflows - from AlphaFold structure retrieval and AlphaGenome variant scoring to ChEMBL bioactivity queries - using modular Antigravity plugins. ### 2. 🔬 Interactive 3D Mol* MCP Sidecars Over Static Plots Scientific discovery requires interactive 3D inspection. I documented how to wire Model Context Protocol (MCP) sidecars with Mol* so agents can load `.pdb`/`.cif` structures, highlight active-site residues, and inspect 3D molecular representations. ### 3. 📦 Self-Contained PEP 723 `uv` Skills & Safety Hooks Every skill in my architecture uses inline PEP 723 dependency metadata executed via `uv`, paired with deterministic `before_tool` credential and safety hooks. --- What happens when you ask an AI coding agent to **score a non-coding human genomic variant with AlphaGenome**, **map a missense mutation onto an AlphaFold 3D protein structure**, **screen ChEMBL for nanomolar small-molecule inhibitors**, or **restore a damaged 2,000-year-old Roman inscription using Google DeepMind's Aeneas model**? If you try to stuff 40 scientific APIs, rate limiters, clinical safety guardrails, and 3D WebGL visualizers into a single mega-prompt, the agent collapses under context bloat and hallucinated parameters. **Google Antigravity** solves this at the runtime level with its **Plugin & Customization Architecture** - combining **Progressive-Disclosure Skills (`SKILL.md`)**, **Always-On Rules (`AGENTS.md`)**, **Lifecycle Hooks (`hooks.json`)**, **Zero-Leak Credential Protocols**, and **Model Context Protocol (`mcp_config.json`) + Background Sidecars (`sidecar.json`)**. Instead of just reading the docs, I explored the newly open-sourced **[Google DeepMind Science Skills (`google-deepmind/science-skills`, `v1.3.1`)](https://github.com/google-deepmind/science-skills)** repository (Apache 2.0 / CC-BY 4.0) and built the open-source **[Antigravity Science Plugin Cookbook & Interactive 3D Studio](https://github.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook)** - complete with a **live browser-based 3D Biomolecular & Variant WebGL Sandbox**, a **zero-dependency PEP 723 3D protein + PAE generator**, and a production **`bio-structural-qc` custom plugin**. --- ## Try the Live 3D Biomolecular & MCP Sidecar Studio in Your Browser * **[Launch the Interactive 3D Biomolecular & Variant WebGL Studio (`index.html`)](https://robinamirbahar.github.io/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/)** * Explore 3D C-alpha backbones & non-covalent contact networks for **TP53 (`AF-P04637`)**, **Crambin (`1CRN`)**, and **EGFR Kinase + Gefitinib (`CHEMBL203`)**. * Click any 3D residue sphere via raycasting to trigger live **`annotate_region`** MCP tool calls, inspect **AlphaFold pLDDT** & **AlphaGenome Variant Impact (AVI)** scores, upload your own `.pdb`/`.cif` files, or run the interactive **Aeneas Latin Epigraphy** restoration demo! * **[Full Source Code & `bio-structural-qc` Plugin on GitHub (`RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook`)](https://github.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook)** --- ## 1. Five Production Engineering Patterns Inside the Science Plugin While inspecting the source files across all 40 skills, five engineering patterns stood out that every Google Cloud and agentic AI builder can adopt. ### Pattern 1: Always-On Behavioral Routing via `rules/AGENTS.md` As documented in the public **[Antigravity Rules Guide (`antigravity.google/docs/rules`)](https://antigravity.google/docs/rules?utm_campaign=deveco_gdemembers&utm_source=deveco)**, rules define persistent coding standards and architectural constraints (`always_on`, `model_decision`, `glob`, or `manual`) across workspace and global scopes. In my custom `bio-structural-qc` plugin (`plugins/bio-structural-qc/rules/AGENTS.md`), I use a compact `AGENTS.md` rule so the agent automatically audits 3D coordinate files (`.pdb`, `.cif`, `.mmcif`) and warns about low-confidence disordered regions before running downstream structural searches or headless PyMOL renders: ```markdown # Biomolecular Structure QC Gate Whenever a workflow downloads or modifies a 3D coordinate file (`.pdb`, `.cif`, or `.mmcif`) for downstream structural analysis, homology search, or variant mapping: 1. **Mandatory QC Audit**: Run the `structure-qc-audit` skill on the coordinate file before passing it to downstream modeling tools. 2. **Disorder Warning**: If more than 30% of alpha-carbon (`CA`) atoms have a B-factor / pLDDT score below `50.0`, explicitly warn the user about disordered or low-confidence regions and report the high-confidence domain boundaries (`pLDDT >= 70`). ``` --- ### Pattern 2: Zero-Pollution Python Micro-Environments (`uv` + PEP 723 + Sliding-Window PAE Math) Running global `pip install` inside a user's repository breaks virtual environments. Instead, every Science skill uses `uv run` with **PEP 723 inline script metadata (`# /// script`)** and enforces rate limits and mathematical heuristics inside deterministic Python scripts. For example, in `skills/alphafold_database_fetch_and_analyze/scripts/`: * `fetch_structure.py` uses `polite-http` with a hard `qps=1.0` rate limit (`CLIENT = http_client.HttpClient("https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk", qps=1.0)`) and automatically falls back to the longest isoform for massive proteins (`> 2,700` amino acids like Dystrophin). * `analyze_pae.py` forbids the LLM from guessing domain boundaries by running a **20-residue sliding-window Predicted Aligned Error (PAE) clustering algorithm** (`distance_cutoff=7.0 Å`, `min_domain_size=40`, `merge_cutoff=15.0 Å`): ```python """Analyzes Predicted Aligned Error (PAE) and detects domain boundaries.""" # /// script # requires-python = ">=3.10" # dependencies = [] # /// def find_sub_domains(pae_matrix, distance_cutoff=7.0, min_domain_size=40): """Identifies structurally independent sub-domains based on the PAE matrix.""" n_res = len(pae_matrix) domains, current_domain = [], [] for i in range(n_res): if not current_domain: current_domain.append(i) continue window_size = min(20, len(current_domain)) recent_res = current_domain[-window_size:] pae_sum = sum(pae_matrix[r][i] + pae_matrix[i][r] for r in recent_res) avg_pae = pae_sum / (2.0 * window_size) if avg_pae < distance_cutoff: current_domain.append(i) else: if len(current_domain) >= min_domain_size: domains.append(current_domain) current_domain = [i] if len(current_domain) >= min_domain_size: domains.append(current_domain) return [[comp[0] + 1, comp[-1] + 1] for comp in domains] ``` --- ### Pattern 3: The Zero-Leak Credential Protocol (`skills/credentials/SKILL.md`) Genomic and literature APIs like **AlphaGenome** (`ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY`) require secret keys. If an agent asks a user to paste their API key into the chat - or runs `cat ~/.env` - that secret is permanently recorded in the conversation transcript and model context. The `credentials` skill solves this with a strict **Zero-Leak Protocol**: 1. **Silent Exit-Code Verification:** The agent checks whether the variable exists in `~/.env` using `grep -sq` (quiet + suppress errors), reading *only* the `0` vs. non-zero exit code: ```bash grep -sq "^ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY=" ~/.env ``` 2. **Hidden Terminal Prompting (`read -s`):** If missing, the agent stops immediately and outputs a terminal command for the user to run locally where keystrokes are hidden (`read -s`): ```bash printf "Enter ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY (typing hidden): " && read -s val && echo && echo "ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY=$val" >> "$HOME/.env" && echo "Saved." ``` 3. **Internal `dotenv` Ingestion:** Helper scripts load `~/.env` internally via `dotenv`, so the key never appears in command-line flags or stdout. --- ### Pattern 4: Background Sidecars (`sidecar.json`) & Custom 3D WebGL / MCP Tool Servers (`mcp_config.json`) As documented in the public **[Antigravity Sidecars Guide (`antigravity.google/docs/sidecars`)](https://antigravity.google/docs/sidecars?utm_campaign=deveco_gdemembers&utm_source=deveco)** and **[MCP Guide (`antigravity.google/docs/mcp`)](https://antigravity.google/docs/mcp?utm_campaign=deveco_gdemembers&utm_source=deveco)**, Antigravity lets plugins pair **Model Context Protocol (`mcp_config.json`)** tool servers with managed background **Sidecar processes (`sidecar.json`)** that support `command`, `builtin` (`schedule`), `args`, `restart_policy` (`always`, `on-failure`, `never`), `description`, `env`, and `display_name`, plus programmatic interaction via `agentapi`. In my open-source **[Antigravity Science Plugin Cookbook](https://github.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook)**, I pair a zero-dependency Python Stdio MCP Server (`plugins/genomics-variant-mcp/mcp_config.json`) with a documented background Sidecar worker (`sidecar.json`) and my browser-based **3D PDBe Mol\* / WebGL Biomolecular Studio (`index.html`)**: ![End-to-End 3D Structural Triage Sequence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/main/assets/arch_3d_sidecar_sequence.png?v=white2) Here are the two standard configuration files documented in `antigravity.google/docs/mcp` and `antigravity.google/docs/sidecars`: * **`mcp_config.json` (connecting a local Stdio MCP server at the plugin root):** ```json { "mcpServers": { "genomics_variant_mcp": { "command": "uv", "args": ["run", "mcp/variant_mcp_server.py"], "timeoutSeconds": 180 } } } ``` * **`sidecars/qc_monitor/sidecar.json` (configuring a managed background sidecar process per `antigravity.google/docs/sidecars`):** ```json { "description": "Background 3D structure QC & artifact monitor", "display_name": "Structure QC Sidecar", "command": "uv", "args": ["run", "worker.py"], "restart_policy": "on-failure" } ``` --- ### Pattern 5: Domain-Specific Guardrails - From Clinical Genetics (`AlphaGenome`) to Ancient Epigraphy (`Aeneas` & `Ithaca`) Two of the most fascinating skills in the bundle demonstrate how `SKILL.md` enforces domain-specific scientific rigor: 1. **`alphagenome-variant-impact-score` (Strict Molecular Framing + Context-Overflow Protection):** * **Clinical Safety Gate:** Explicitly forbids extrapolating high AlphaGenome Variant Impact (AVI) scores into clinical diagnoses or patient prognosis, restricting outputs to molecular mechanisms (splicing disruption, chromatin accessibility, TF binding, or GENCODE v46 transcript coordinates). * **Stdout Overflow Guard:** Warns the agent that `--include_track_info --format json` emits `~3.9 KB` per variant, requiring direct file redirection (`-o query_results.json`) whenever querying `> 3` variants so stdout never floods the context window. 2. **`predictingthepast` (Ancient Latin & Greek Epigraphy with DeepMind's Aeneas & Ithaca):** * Restores damaged ancient inscriptions, attributes geographical province + chronological date ranges, and finds parallel inscriptions using special gap syntax (`?` for a single missing character, `#` for an unknown-length damaged gap): ```bash uv run scripts/preprocess.py --language=latin --input="imp caesar divi f ???????? cos xi" ``` * Enforces a **Self-Contained Epigraphy Rule**: forbids the agent from using web search to "cheat" or override the neural restoration probabilities returned by Aeneas/Ithaca. --- ## 4. Five End-to-End Multi-Skill Use Cases Across the 40 Science Skills Because all 40 skills share the conversation's artifact directory, Antigravity can chain multiple domain-specific CLI scripts and MCP sidecars in a single research session. I included a runnable benchmark suite in [`examples/multi_domain_science_use_cases.py`](https://github.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/blob/main/examples/multi_domain_science_use_cases.py) (`uv run examples/multi_domain_science_use_cases.py`) that executes and scores all five multi-skill pipelines below: ![5 End-to-End Multi-Skill Pipelines Scorecard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/main/examples/generated_use_cases/science_use_cases_scorecard.png?v=white2) --- ### Use Case 1: Precision Oncology & 3D Pocket Triage (`ClinVar` → `gnomAD` → `AlphaFold` → `ChEMBL` → `PyMOL / 3D WebGL Studio`) **Scenario:** A translational oncology team wants to evaluate an **EGFR L858R** (`rs121434568`, `chr7:55191822:T>G`) driver mutation, verify gene loss-of-function constraint, inspect 3D active-site confidence, rank nanomolar kinase inhibitors, and highlight the pocket in 3D. ```bash # 1. Check allele rarity & gene constraint (pLI / LOEUF) in gnomAD uv run ~/.gemini/config/plugins/science/skills/gnomad_database/scripts/get_gene_constraint.py \ --gene EGFR --output ./artifacts/egfr_constraint.json # 2. Fetch AlphaFold 3D structure (P00533) & audit pLDDT + PAE domains uv run ~/.gemini/config/plugins/science/skills/alphafold_database_fetch_and_analyze/scripts/fetch_structure.py \ P00533 -o ./artifacts/P00533/ uv run ~/.gemini/config/plugins/science/skills/alphafold_database_fetch_and_analyze/scripts/analyze_pae.py \ ./artifacts/P00533/AF-P00533-F1-predicted_aligned_error_v6.json # 3. Screen ChEMBL for EGFR (CHEMBL203) bioactivities & download 3D SDF ligands uv run ~/.gemini/config/plugins/science/skills/chembl_database/scripts/chembl_api.py \ activity --search "EGFR" --limit 10 --output ./artifacts/egfr_chembl_ic50.json uv run ~/.gemini/config/plugins/science/skills/chembl_database/scripts/chembl_api.py \ molecule --id CHEMBL939 --dl_format sdf --output ./artifacts/gefitinib.sdf ``` Finally, the agent renders the 3D kinase pocket (`residues 855-862` in chain `A`) using headless PyMOL (`pymol` skill) or my interactive **[3D Biomolecular & Variant WebGL Studio (`index.html`)](https://robinamirbahar.github.io/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/)**: ![Use Case 1 - Precision Oncology & 3D Kinase Pocket Triage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/main/examples/generated_use_cases/uc1_precision_oncology_3d.png?v=white2) --- ### Use Case 2: Non-Coding GWAS Enhancer Variant Triage (`AlphaGenome` → `UCSC phyloP` → `ENCODE cCRE` → `JASPAR` → `GTEx`) **Scenario:** Over 90% of GWAS risk loci fall in non-coding DNA. Suppose you are investigating `chr1:109274968:G>T` (`rs12740374` at the *SORT1* 1p13 locus) and want to know *how* it alters gene regulation across human tissues without hallucinating clinical diagnoses: ```bash # 1. Score variant impact across 18 biological modalities + GENCODE v46 coordinates uv run ~/.gemini/config/plugins/science/skills/alphagenome_variant_impact_score/scripts/alphagenome_atlas_avi.py \ query "chr1:109274968:G>T" --include_track_info --format json -o ./artifacts/sort1_avi.json # 2. Check 100-vertebrate evolutionary constraint (phyloP100way & phastCons100way) uv run ~/.gemini/config/plugins/science/skills/ucsc_conservation_and_tfbs/scripts/get_conservation.py \ --coordinates "chr1:109274968" --output ./artifacts/sort1_phylop.json # 3. Fetch Transcription Factor Position Weight Matrices (PWMs) from JASPAR (CEBPA) uv run ~/.gemini/config/plugins/science/skills/jaspar_database/scripts/jaspar_cli.py \ search --query "CEBPA" --output ./artifacts/cebpa_jaspar.json ``` * **Engineering Guardrail in Action:** The `alphagenome-variant-impact-score` skill enforces that `--include_track_info` outputs (`~3.9 KB/variant`) are redirected via `-o` and framed strictly in terms of molecular mechanisms (`CEBPA` binding site creation + liver RNA-seq eQTL shift): ![Use Case 2 - Non-Coding GWAS Enhancer Variant Triage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/main/examples/generated_use_cases/uc2_noncoding_alphagenome.png?v=white2) --- ### Use Case 3: Dark-Proteome Enzyme Discovery (`AlphaFold` → `Foldseek 3D Search` → `InterPro` → `Clustal Omega MSA` → `Headless PyMOL`) **Scenario:** A protein engineering group wants to discover novel thermostable plastic-degrading **PETase** homologs hidden in environmental metagenomes where sequence identity is below 25% (the "twilight zone" where BLAST fails, but 3D fold geometry is conserved): ```bash # 1. Search the 3D coordinate file against Foldseek's metagenomic & AlphaFold databases uv run ~/.gemini/config/plugins/science/skills/foldseek_structural_search/scripts/search.py \ ./artifacts/PETase_AF.cif \ --databases afdb50,mgnify_esm30,pdb100,cath50 \ -o ./artifacts/petase_foldseek.json > ./artifacts/petase_foldseek_summary.md # 2. Reproducibility Lifecycle Hook (`hooks.json` & `log_reproducibility_audit.py`) A bare timestamp log only tells you *when* `run_command` fired, not *what* actually executed or which version of a script and input `.pdb`/`.cif` coordinates produced a scientific result. At the same time, logging raw shell commands is dangerous if an inline environment variable or `--api-key` flag is present. Because Antigravity passes a structured JSON payload to every `PostToolUse` hook over `stdin` (`toolCall.args.CommandLine`, `workspacePaths`, `conversationId`, `stepIdx`), I wire `plugins/bio-structural-qc/hooks.json` to a zero-dependency PEP 723 audit script (`plugins/bio-structural-qc/scripts/log_reproducibility_audit.py`) that: 1. **Redacts Secrets Before Logging:** Strips any environment variables matching `*KEY*`, `*TOKEN*`, `*SECRET*`, `*PASS*`, `*CRED*`, or `*AUTH*`, plus `Bearer`/`Basic` headers and `--api-key`/`--token` CLI flags. 2. **Records Exact Script Versions & Git State:** Captures `git rev-parse --short HEAD` (`+dirty` if uncommitted changes exist) and computes a 16-character SHA-256 digest (`script_versions`) for every executed `.py` or `.sh` script. 3. **Hashes All Referenced Input & Output Files:** Tokenizes the command line and computes SHA-256 digests (`file_hashes`) for every referenced `.pdb`, `.cif`, `.mmcif`, `.vcf`, `.json`, `.fasta`, or `.sdf` file. 4. **Honors the `PostToolUse` Stdout Contract:** Appends the JSONL record to `~/.gemini/qc_command_audit.jsonl` and emits `{}` on `stdout`. * **`plugins/bio-structural-qc/hooks.json`:** ```json { "qc-command-audit-log": { "enabled": true, "PostToolUse": [ { "matcher": "run_command", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "uv run plugins/bio-structural-qc/scripts/log_reproducibility_audit.py", "timeout": 5 } ] } ] } } ``` * **`plugins/bio-structural-qc/scripts/log_reproducibility_audit.py` (Core Redaction & Hashing Logic):** ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """PostToolUse reproducibility hook: logs redacted commands, script SHA-256 versions, and input file hashes.""" # /// script # requires-python = ">=3.10" # dependencies = [] # /// import datetime, hashlib, json, pathlib, re, shlex, subprocess, sys SECRET_PATTERNS = [ (re.compile(r"\b([A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASS|PASSWORD|CRED|AUTH)[A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*=\s*('[^']*'|\"[^\"]*\"|\S+)", re.I), r"\1=[REDACTED]"), (re.compile(r"(Bearer|Basic)\s+[A-Za-z0-9._\-+/=]+", re.I), r"\1 [REDACTED]"), (re.compile(r"(--(?:api[-_]?key|token|secret|password)|x-goog-api-key:|api-key:)\s*([=:]?\s*)('[^']*'|\"[^\"]*\"|\S+)", re.I), r"\1\2[REDACTED]"), ] TRACKED_EXTENSIONS = {".py", ".sh", ".pdb", ".cif", ".mmcif", ".json", ".fasta", ".fa", ".aln", ".sdf", ".vcf", ".gtf", ".tsv", ".csv"} def redact_secrets(cmd: str) -> str: for pattern, repl in SECRET_PATTERNS: cmd = pattern.sub(repl, cmd) return cmd def sha256_file(path: pathlib.Path) -> str: h = hashlib.sha256() with path.open("rb") as f: for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(65536), b""): h.update(chunk) return f"sha256:{h.hexdigest()[:16]}" ``` #### Verified Commands: Test Secret Redaction & Input File Hashing Locally You can verify both the built-in `--self-test` mode and the live `stdin` hook contract in two commands: ```bash # Five Production Engineering Patterns Inside the Science Plugin While inspecting the source files across all 40 skills, five engineering patterns stood out that every Google Cloud and agentic AI builder can adopt. ### Pattern 1: Always-On Behavioral Routing via `rules/AGENTS.md` As documented in the public **[Antigravity Rules Guide (`antigravity.google/docs/rules`)](https://antigravity.google/docs/rules?utm_campaign=deveco_gdemembers&utm_source=deveco)**, rules define persistent coding standards and architectural constraints (`always_on`, `model_decision`, `glob`, or `manual`) across workspace and global scopes. In my custom `bio-structural-qc` plugin (`plugins/bio-structural-qc/rules/AGENTS.md`), I use a compact `AGENTS.md` rule so the agent automatically audits 3D coordinate files (`.pdb`, `.cif`, `.mmcif`) and warns about low-confidence disordered regions before running downstream structural searches or headless PyMOL renders: ```markdown # Biomolecular Structure QC Gate Whenever a workflow downloads or modifies a 3D coordinate file (`.pdb`, `.cif`, or `.mmcif`) for downstream structural analysis, homology search, or variant mapping: 1. **Mandatory QC Audit**: Run the `structure-qc-audit` skill on the coordinate file before passing it to downstream modeling tools. 2. **Disorder Warning**: If more than 30% of alpha-carbon (`CA`) atoms have a B-factor / pLDDT score below `50.0`, explicitly warn the user about disordered or low-confidence regions and report the high-confidence domain boundaries (`pLDDT >= 70`). ``` --- ### Pattern 2: Zero-Pollution Python Micro-Environments (`uv` + PEP 723 + Sliding-Window PAE Math) Running global `pip install` inside a user's repository breaks virtual environments. Instead, every Science skill uses `uv run` with **PEP 723 inline script metadata (`# /// script`)** and enforces rate limits and mathematical heuristics inside deterministic Python scripts. For example, in `skills/alphafold_database_fetch_and_analyze/scripts/`: * `fetch_structure.py` uses `polite-http` with a hard `qps=1.0` rate limit (`CLIENT = http_client.HttpClient("https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk", qps=1.0)`) and automatically falls back to the longest isoform for massive proteins (`> 2,700` amino acids like Dystrophin). * `analyze_pae.py` forbids the LLM from guessing domain boundaries by running a **20-residue sliding-window Predicted Aligned Error (PAE) clustering algorithm** (`distance_cutoff=7.0 Å`, `min_domain_size=40`, `merge_cutoff=15.0 Å`): ```python """Analyzes Predicted Aligned Error (PAE) and detects domain boundaries.""" # /// script # requires-python = ">=3.10" # dependencies = [] # /// def find_sub_domains(pae_matrix, distance_cutoff=7.0, min_domain_size=40): """Identifies structurally independent sub-domains based on the PAE matrix.""" n_res = len(pae_matrix) domains, current_domain = [], [] for i in range(n_res): if not current_domain: current_domain.append(i) continue window_size = min(20, len(current_domain)) recent_res = current_domain[-window_size:] pae_sum = sum(pae_matrix[r][i] + pae_matrix[i][r] for r in recent_res) avg_pae = pae_sum / (2.0 * window_size) if avg_pae < distance_cutoff: current_domain.append(i) else: if len(current_domain) >= min_domain_size: domains.append(current_domain) current_domain = [i] if len(current_domain) >= min_domain_size: domains.append(current_domain) return [[comp[0] + 1, comp[-1] + 1] for comp in domains] ``` --- ### Pattern 3: The Zero-Leak Credential Protocol (`skills/credentials/SKILL.md`) Genomic and literature APIs like **AlphaGenome** (`ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY`) require secret keys. If an agent asks a user to paste their API key into the chat - or runs `cat ~/.env` - that secret is permanently recorded in the conversation transcript and model context. The `credentials` skill solves this with a strict **Zero-Leak Protocol**: 1. **Silent Exit-Code Verification:** The agent checks whether the variable exists in `~/.env` using `grep -sq` (quiet + suppress errors), reading *only* the `0` vs. non-zero exit code: ```bash grep -sq "^ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY=" ~/.env ``` 2. **Hidden Terminal Prompting (`read -s`):** If missing, the agent stops immediately and outputs a terminal command for the user to run locally where keystrokes are hidden (`read -s`): ```bash printf "Enter ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY (typing hidden): " && read -s val && echo && echo "ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY=$val" >> "$HOME/.env" && echo "Saved." ``` 3. **Internal `dotenv` Ingestion:** Helper scripts load `~/.env` internally via `dotenv`, so the key never appears in command-line flags or stdout. --- ### Pattern 4: Background Sidecars (`sidecar.json`) & Custom 3D WebGL / MCP Tool Servers (`mcp_config.json`) As documented in the public **[Antigravity Sidecars Guide (`antigravity.google/docs/sidecars`)](https://antigravity.google/docs/sidecars?utm_campaign=deveco_gdemembers&utm_source=deveco)** and **[MCP Guide (`antigravity.google/docs/mcp`)](https://antigravity.google/docs/mcp?utm_campaign=deveco_gdemembers&utm_source=deveco)**, Antigravity lets plugins pair **Model Context Protocol (`mcp_config.json`)** tool servers with managed background **Sidecar processes (`sidecar.json`)** that support `command`, `builtin` (`schedule`), `args`, `restart_policy` (`always`, `on-failure`, `never`), `description`, `env`, and `display_name`, plus programmatic interaction via `agentapi`. Reproducibility Lifecycle Hook (`hooks.json` & `log_reproducibility_audit.py`) A bare timestamp log only tells you *when* `run_command` fired, not *what* actually executed or which version of a script and input `.pdb`/`.cif` coordinates produced a scientific result. At the same time, logging raw shell commands is dangerous if an inline environment variable or `--api-key` flag is present. Because Antigravity passes a structured JSON payload to every `PostToolUse` hook over `stdin` (`toolCall.args.CommandLine`, `workspacePaths`, `conversationId`, `stepIdx`), I wire `plugins/bio-structural-qc/hooks.json` to a zero-dependency PEP 723 audit script (`plugins/bio-structural-qc/scripts/log_reproducibility_audit.py`) that: 1. **Redacts Secrets Before Logging:** Strips any environment variables matching `*KEY*`, `*TOKEN*`, `*SECRET*`, `*PASS*`, `*CRED*`, or `*AUTH*`, plus `Bearer`/`Basic` headers and `--api-key`/`--token` CLI flags. 2. **Records Exact Script Versions & Git State:** Captures `git rev-parse --short HEAD` (`+dirty` if uncommitted changes exist) and computes a 16-character SHA-256 digest (`script_versions`) for every executed `.py` or `.sh` script. 3. **Hashes All Referenced Input & Output Files:** Tokenizes the command line and computes SHA-256 digests (`file_hashes`) for every referenced `.pdb`, `.cif`, `.mmcif`, `.vcf`, `.json`, `.fasta`, or `.sdf` file. 4. **Honors the `PostToolUse` Stdout Contract:** Appends the JSONL record to `~/.gemini/qc_command_audit.jsonl` and emits `{}` on `stdout`. * **`plugins/bio-structural-qc/hooks.json`:** ```json { "qc-command-audit-log": { "enabled": true, "PostToolUse": [ { "matcher": "run_command", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "uv run plugins/bio-structural-qc/scripts/log_reproducibility_audit.py", "timeout": 5 } ] } ] } } ``` * **`plugins/bio-structural-qc/scripts/log_reproducibility_audit.py` (Core Redaction & Hashing Logic):** ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """PostToolUse reproducibility hook: logs redacted commands, script SHA-256 versions, and input file hashes.""" # /// script # requires-python = ">=3.10" # dependencies = [] # /// import datetime, hashlib, json, pathlib, re, shlex, subprocess, sys SECRET_PATTERNS = [ (re.compile(r"\b([A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASS|PASSWORD|CRED|AUTH)[A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*=\s*('[^']*'|\"[^\"]*\"|\S+)", re.I), r"\1=[REDACTED]"), (re.compile(r"(Bearer|Basic)\s+[A-Za-z0-9._\-+/=]+", re.I), r"\1 [REDACTED]"), (re.compile(r"(--(?:api[-_]?key|token|secret|password)|x-goog-api-key:|api-key:)\s*([=:]?\s*)('[^']*'|\"[^\"]*\"|\S+)", re.I), r"\1\2[REDACTED]"), ] TRACKED_EXTENSIONS = {".py", ".sh", ".pdb", ".cif", ".mmcif", ".json", ".fasta", ".fa", ".aln", ".sdf", ".vcf", ".gtf", ".tsv", ".csv"} def redact_secrets(cmd: str) -> str: for pattern, repl in SECRET_PATTERNS: cmd = pattern.sub(repl, cmd) return cmd def sha256_file(path: pathlib.Path) -> str: h = hashlib.sha256() with path.open("rb") as f: for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(65536), b""): h.update(chunk) return f"sha256:{h.hexdigest()[:16]}" ``` #### Verified Commands: Test Secret Redaction & Input File Hashing Locally You can verify both the built-in `--self-test` mode and the live `stdin` hook contract in two commands: ```bash # The 4 Documented `mcp_config.json` Patterns 1. **Pattern 1 - Local Stdio Subprocess (`command` + `args` + `env`):** Spawns a local MCP process over `stdio` using `uv`, `node`, `python3`, or `dart` (for example, my cookbook's `genomics_variant_mcp` server or local SQLite/file-system explorers). 2. **Pattern 2 - Google-Credentials Authenticated HTTP (`authProviderType: "google_credentials"`):** Connects directly to managed Google Cloud and developer MCP endpoints (such as **BigQuery**, **AlloyDB for PostgreSQL**, **Spanner**, **Cloud SQL**, **Bigtable**, **Dataplex**, and **Google Developer Knowledge** at `https://developerknowledge.googleapis.com/mcp`) using local Application Default Credentials (`gcloud auth application-default login`). 3. **Pattern 3 - Remote Streamable HTTP with Custom Headers (`serverUrl` + `headers` + `timeoutSeconds`):** Connects to remote Streamable HTTP MCP endpoints (such as `https://gemini-api-docs-mcp.dev` for `gemini_search_docs` and `gemini_get_doc`) with custom `Authorization` headers and configurable timeouts (`timeoutSeconds: 600`). 4. **Pattern 4 - OAuth 2.0 Remote Servers (Dynamic Client Registration or Manual `oauth` Object):** Authenticates against remote SaaS and enterprise MCP servers using automatic OAuth Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) or a manual `oauth` (`clientId`, `clientSecret`) configuration redirecting to `https://antigravity.google/oauth-callback`. ### B. Starter Plugin #2: `plugins/genomics-variant-mcp` (Custom Python Stdio MCP Server + Specialist Subagent) To show how to package your own **MCP server** and **Specialist Subagent** inside an Antigravity plugin, the cookbook includes **[`plugins/genomics-variant-mcp`](https://github.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/tree/main/plugins/genomics-variant-mcp)**: * **[`mcp_config.json`](https://github.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/blob/main/plugins/genomics-variant-mcp/mcp_config.json)** - Registers `genomics_variant_mcp` via `uv run mcp/variant_mcp_server.py` and marks both tools as `"eager": true` so they load directly into the agent's native tool declarations: ```json { "mcpServers": { "genomics_variant_mcp": { "command": "uv", "args": ["run", "mcp/variant_mcp_server.py"], "tools": [ { "name": "score_variant_impact", "eager": true }, { "name": "evaluate_lipinski_ro5", "eager": true } ] } } } ``` * **[`mcp/variant_mcp_server.py`](https://github.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/blob/main/plugins/genomics-variant-mcp/mcp/variant_mcp_server.py)** - A zero-dependency PEP 723 JSON-RPC 2.0 Stdio MCP server implementing `initialize`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call` for: * `score_variant_impact`: Scores 1-based `chr:pos:ref>alt` SNVs (transition/transversion class, predicted AlphaGenome AVI impact score, PhyloP 100-way conservation, and molecular priority). * `evaluate_lipinski_ro5`: Evaluates small-molecule leads against Lipinski's Rule of Five (`MW ≤ 500`, `LogP ≤ 5`, `HBD ≤ 5`, `HBA ≤ 10`) and Veber's polar surface area rule (`PSA ≤ 140 Å²`). * **[`agents/clinical-variant-curator.md`](https://github.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/blob/main/plugins/genomics-variant-mcp/agents/clinical-variant-curator.md)** - A specialist subagent (modeled on `firebase`'s `agents/firestore-rules-author.md`) with YAML frontmatter (`mainAgent: true`, `subagent: true`, `commandExecutionPolicy: auto`) that enforces research-only molecular framing. Run its built-in self-test with `uv`: ```bash uv run plugins/genomics-variant-mcp/mcp/variant_mcp_server.py --self-test ``` ### C. Starter Plugin #3: `plugins/epigraphy-citation-kit` (Ancient Epigraphy Validator + `PreToolUse` Hook) The third starter plugin, **[`plugins/epigraphy-citation-kit`](https://github.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/tree/main/plugins/epigraphy-citation-kit)**, pairs a `PreToolUse` lifecycle hook (`hooks.json`) with a PEP 723 Leiden bracket normalizer ([`validate_epigraphy.py`](https://github.com/RobinaMirbahar/antigravity-science-plugin-cookbook/blob/main/plugins/epigraphy-citation-kit/skills/epigraphy-gap-validator/scripts/validate_epigraphy.py)) that automatically converts standard Leiden epigraphic brackets (`[---]` and `[...]`) into DeepMind Aeneas/Ithaca `#` and `?` tokens, checks for forbidden `##` or `?#` sequences, and pads short inscriptions to the 25-character minimum: ```bash uv run plugins/epigraphy-citation-kit/skills/epigraphy-gap-validator/scripts/validate_epigraphy.py \ --text "IMP CAESAR DIVI F [---] COS [...] III" --language latin ``` --- ## 7.
